record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Functional Analysis and Function Theory
record.original_question: Let K be a compact subset of R^n such that for each hyperplane T in R^n the intersection T ∩ K is (m-1)-convex. Find an additional condition on K that, together with this hyperplane-section hypothesis, is sufficient to guarantee that K itself is m-convex.

evidence.quote: Definition 16.1. A compact K ⊂ Rn is called to be m-convex (m < n) if for each x ∈ Rn \ K there exists an m-plane T(x) such that x ∈ T(x) and T(x) ∩ K = ∅.

Problem 16.3. Let K ⊂ Rn be a compact. Suppose that for each hyperplane T ⊂ Rn the intersection T ∩K is (m−1)-convex. Find a condition on K which together with the above one would be sufficient for K to be m-convex.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Definition. For an integer m with 1 ≤ m < n, a compact set K ⊂ R^n is called m-convex if for every point x ∈ R^n \ K there exists an affine m-dimensional plane T(x) ⊂ R^n with x ∈ T(x) and T(x) ∩ K = ∅.

Problem. Let K ⊂ R^n be a compact set such that for every affine hyperplane T ⊂ R^n the intersection T ∩ K is (m−1)-convex (as a compact subset of T ≅ R^{n−1}, in the sense above). Find an additional geometric or topological condition on K which, combined with this hyperplane-section hypothesis, is sufficient to ensure that K itself is m-convex.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches for results characterizing m-convexity of compacta in R^n via (m−1)-convexity of hyperplane sections did not return relevant literature, so the problem's status could not be confirmed.
